issues.title: [Bug]: toBalString of negative infinity produces invalid expression `float:-Infinity`
issues.reasoning: lang.value toBalString (expression-style ToString, spec §5.9.5) must yield a valid Ballerina expression; `float:-Infinity` does not parse, correct is `-float:Infinity`. Clean-context spec check: VALID-BUG. Note: corpus tobalstring-v.bal:71 and its txtar codify the wrong output and need updating with the fix. No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: float:round(x, fractionDigits) rounds the decimal string instead of the exact binary value
issues.reasoning: lang.float round(x, fractionDigits) must round the exact binary value (closest multiple of 10^-fractionDigits to x); 2.675/0.15/0.35 are strictly below the midpoint so 2.67/0.1/0.3 are expected. Clean-context spec check: VALID-BUG. Related to but distinct from #1029 (another round(fractionDigits) precision bug); not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: Including an inclusive (open) record in an exclusive record drops the implicit `anydata...` rest descriptor
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected never, got 3
  --> i1452.bal:13:41
   |
13 |     Derived d = {x: 1, y: "hello", "z": 3};
   |                                         ^

ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.reasoning: §5.4.2.2: an included inclusive record is treated as having an explicit `anydata...` rest descriptor which is carried into the including type unless overridden, so Derived is open and `"z": 3` is valid. Type checker rejects a valid program (`expected never`). Clean-context spec check: VALID-BUG. Issue reports the runtime inherent type is also closed; root cause is the type resolution of the inclusion. No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: XML template drops whitespace text that follows a processing instruction
issues.reasoning: §6.6.2: xml template content is parsed with the XML `content` production, so whitespace after a PI is CharData and must be kept as a text item. xml:fromString keeps it, so the bug is in the template parsing/lowering path in the front end. Clean-context spec check: VALID-BUG. Related XML-template issues (#1091, #1226, #1412) cover other cases; not duplicates.

issues.title: [Bug]: range expression used as a value crashes the compiler (INTERNAL_ERROR: unexpected binary operator kind: ..<)
issues.output:
fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: unexpected binary operator kind: ..<
 --> i1454.bal:4:13
  |
4 |     var r = 1 ..< 3;
  |             ^^^^^^^

ballerina: BIR generation failed
issues.reasoning: §6.26: a range-expr yields an object belonging to Iterable<int,()> and may be used outside foreach. BIR generation fails with fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR] on a valid program. That is a diagnostic, not a Go panic, so frontend-crash is not added. Clean-context spec check: VALID-BUG. Related: #1349 (foreach over range binding type) and #1302; neither is a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: isolated class accepts non-private fields that are not isolated (only `public` fields are checked)
issues.reasoning: §8.6 + §6.8.1: in an isolated class, any field that is not isolated (final with a readonly/isolated-object type) must be private. `int count` and `final int[] items` must be rejected, but the program compiles and prints 5. Clean-context spec check: VALID-BUG. #1431/#1432 touch the same check in the opposite direction (too strict); not duplicates.

issues.title: [Bug]: source text is not normalized: CR/CRLF kept inside string templates and a leading BOM is a syntax error
issues.reasoning: Spec lexical structure: a leading BOM must be removed and CR/CRLF normalized to LF before parsing. Both are missing: a CRLF template keeps CR (length 4) and a BOM gives SYNTAX_ERROR. Clean-context spec check: VALID-BUG (both parts). No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: relational and `==`/`!=` expressions on singleton operands are not singleton-typed
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected true, got boolean
 --> i1457.bal:7:20
  |
7 |     true ordered = MIN < MAX;
  |                    ^^^^^^^^^

error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected true, got boolean
  --> i1457.bal:10:17
   |
10 |     true same = MIN == 1;
   |                 ^^^^^^^^

error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected false, got boolean
  --> i1457.bal:13:16
   |
13 |     false lt = 2.0 < 1.0;
   |                ^^^^^^^^^

error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected string, got 0|"ordered"
  --> i1457.bal:16:20
   |
16 |     string label = MIN <= MAX ? "ordered" : 0;
   |                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.reasoning: §6.2.4/§6.27/§6.29/§6.32: relational and ==/!= expressions with singleton operands must have a singleton boolean type, and a conditional whose condition has type `true` takes the true branch's type. The type checker gives plain boolean and rejects the valid program. Clean-context spec check: VALID-BUG. Same rule as #1262 (multiplicative/shift/bitwise ops), which is a sibling rather than a duplicate. A shared parent could be considered, but none exists.

issues.title: [Bug]: service declaration evaluates all listener expressions before constructing the service and attaching
issues.output:
listener init one
listener init two
error: attach failed one
issues.reasoning: §8.3.2: the service object is constructed first, then each listener expression is evaluated and attached in turn; a failed attach fails module init before later listener expressions are evaluated. Nutcracker evaluates all listeners first, because desugar/desugar.go hoistInlineServiceListeners hoists them into module listener variables. Desugaring is part of the front end and the generated BIR has the wrong evaluation order. Clean-context spec check: VALID-BUG. No duplicate found.
